mainTopic: רבה בר ירמיה's two 'unsolvable' ברייתות (מרקוליס stones; tree care in שביעית and חול המועד) and breaking or throwing a stick before an idol
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא that רבה בר ירמיה brought. Stones a gentile took from a מרקוליס pile and paved with are permitted, but if a Jew did it they are forbidden. רבה בר ירמיה said no scholar could resolve it. רב ששת explains that the problem is רב גידל's rule that an idol offering can never be permitted. He answers that this rule covers only things like offerings in the בית המקדש, and stones are not such things. Next comes a second ברייתא from רבה בר ירמיה about caring for trees during שביעית and חול המועד, with the same dare. רבינא tests several possible difficulties and knocks each one down, using the rule that preserving a tree is allowed while improving it is forbidden. רב סמא then reveals the real puzzle: on חול המועד, smearing oil is allowed but manuring is forbidden, even though both only preserve the tree. Finally, רב rules that breaking a stick before a stick-worshipped idol makes one liable but throwing it does not. רבא defends this to אביי, and אביי begins a new challenge from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא about stones from a מרקוליס pile
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. A gentile's stones from מרקוליס are permitted, but if a Jew paves roads with them they are forbidden. רבה בר ירמיה adds that no scholar can resolve this ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If a gentile did it,] they are permitted. If a Jew brought stones from the מרקוליס pile and paved paths and streets with them, they are forbidden. And there is no carpenter, nor son of a carpenter, who can resolve this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about stones taken from a מרקוליס idol pile and then presents a dare that no one can explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a gentile uses the stones for paving, he cancels their idol status, so they become permitted. A Jew cannot cancel idol status, so the stones he uses stay forbidden. The closing line warns that something in this ruling is hard to explain, which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Mercury, an idol worshipped by throwing stones onto a pile
Literally 'carpenter'; here it is a nickname for a sharp scholar
To resolve or 'take apart' a difficulty

phrases.english: they are permitted,
A Jew who brought stones from the Mercury pile
and paved paths and streets with them —
they are forbidden,
and there is no carpenter, nor son of a carpenter,
phrases.notes: 'Carpenter' means a scholar, and 'son of a carpenter' means a scholar whose father was also a scholar.

phrases.english: who can resolve it.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולית נגר ולא בר נגר דיפרקינה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gentile can cancel the idol status of מרקוליס stones by paving with them, but a Jew cannot, so the Jew's stones remain forbidden.

steps.title: רב ששת steps up and identifies the difficulty
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says he will resolve the problem himself. He first pinpoints the difficulty: it comes from רב גידל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: I am not a carpenter, nor the son of a carpenter, and yet I will resolve it. What is his difficulty? The rule of רב גידל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת accepts the dare and first names exactly what bothers רבה בר ירמיה. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל taught that a תקרובת עבודה זרה can never have its forbidden status cancelled. Stones thrown onto the מרקוליס pile look like an offering to that idol. So how could a gentile cancel their status and make them permitted?

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to an idol, which can never lose its forbidden status

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not saying the ruling is wrong. He is explaining why it seems to clash with רב גידל's rule, so that he can then remove the clash.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
I am not a carpenter,
nor am I the son of a carpenter,
and yet I will resolve it:
What is his difficulty?
That of Rav Giddel.
phrases.notes: This refers to רב גידל's rule that an offering to an idol can never lose its forbidden status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the dare in step 1 by naming the source of the difficulty
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly makes the ברייתא hard to explain?
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission given to stones a gentile paved with
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stones are an idol offering, רב גידל's rule says they can never be permitted.

steps.title: An offering must resemble one brought inside the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: Something counts as a forbidden idol offering only if it is like an offering in the בית המקדש. Stones are never offered there, so רב גידל's rule does not apply to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: I require it to be like an offering inside the בית המקדש, and there is no such thing here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives his answer. Stones on the מרקוליס pile do not count as a תקרובת, so רב גידל's rule never applies to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item only gets the strict, permanent status of a תקרובת if it is something that would be offered inside the בית המקדש. No one offers stones in the בית המקדש. The stones are still connected to idol worship, but their status is the kind that a gentile can cancel. That is why paving by a gentile makes them permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Like an offering brought inside the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: An item is a permanent, uncancellable idol offering only if it resembles a בית המקדש offering. Stones do not, so a gentile can cancel their status.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general limit on רב גידל's strict rule. Only offerings that resemble Temple service become permanently forbidden.

phrases.english: I require something like what is done inside,
phrases.notes: 'Inside' means inside the בית המקדש: an offering of the kind brought there.

phrases.english: and there is no such thing here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any stone thrown to מרקוליס counts as a permanent idol offering under רב גידל's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only things resembling בית המקדש offerings are permanent idol offerings, so stones can have their status cancelled.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: removing worms and applying manure
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר אבא reports another ברייתא from רבה בר ירמיה. During שביעית you may remove worms from a tree and put manure on its wound, but during חול המועד you may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר אבא said: רבה בר ירמיה came to our place and brought a ברייתא with him. One may remove worms and apply manure during שביעית, but one may not remove worms or apply manure during חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting another ברייתא that רבה בר ירמיה brought, about caring for trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats tree care differently in שביעית and in חול המועד. רבה בר ירמיה will again say no one can explain it. The גמרא then has to work out which part of the ruling is the real difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: Smearing manure on a cut in a tree
חול המועד, the intermediate days of a festival

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Abba said:
Rabba bar Yirmeya happened to come to our place,
and he came and brought a ברייתא with him:
One may remove worms and apply manure during the Sabbatical Year,
but one may not remove worms or apply manure during the intermediate festival days.

steps.triggerLanguage: איקלע רבה בר ירמיה לאתרין ואתא ואייתי מתניתא בידיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the same source, רבה בר ירמיה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing worms and applying manure to trees is allowed during שביעית but forbidden during חול המועד.

steps.title: Pruning is forbidden in both, oiling a pruned spot is allowed in both
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Pruning is forbidden during both שביעית and חול המועד, but smearing oil on a pruned spot is allowed in both. Again, no scholar can resolve the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: In both cases one may not prune. But one may smear oil on a pruned spot, both during חול המועד and during שביעית. And there is no carpenter, nor son of a carpenter, who can resolve this.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with two rules that apply equally to both times. It then closes with the same dare that no scholar can explain it, which sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pruning is real tree work, so it is forbidden in both periods. Smearing oil on a cut only protects the tree from damage, so it is allowed in both. רבה בר ירמיה does not say what the difficulty is. The steps that follow search for it, and step 15 finds it.

keyTerms.meaning: On the pruned spot of a tree

phrases.english: Both here and there, one may not prune,
phrases.notes: 'Here and there' means both during שביעית and during חול המועד.

phrases.english: but one may smear oil on the pruned spot,
both during the intermediate festival days and during the Sabbatical Year.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵית נַגָּר וְלָא בַּר נַגָּר דְּיִפְרְקִינַּהּ.
phrases.english: And there is no carpenter, nor son of a carpenter, who can resolve it.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולית נגר ולא בר נגר דיפרקינה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 4 and repeats the dare
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pruning is forbidden in both periods. Smearing oil on a pruned spot is permitted in both.

steps.title: רבינא offers to solve it and asks what the problem is
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says he is no great scholar but will resolve the ברייתא. First he asks what exactly bothered רבה בר ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: I am not a carpenter or the son of a carpenter, but I will solve it. What was bothering him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא volunteers to solve the puzzle and first asks what the difficulty actually was. This sets up the next steps, where he tries out possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר ירמיה never said what the problem in the ברייתא was. Before רבינא can solve it, he has to identify it. He does this by testing several options and ruling them out one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Carpenter. Here it is an image for a sharp scholar who can 'fix' a hard text.
I will resolve or untangle it.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
I am not a carpenter
phrases.notes: This answers רבה בר ירמיה's line in step 5 that no 'carpenter' could solve it. He means a sharp scholar.

phrases.english: nor am I the son of a carpenter,
and yet I will resolve it:
What is difficult for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 that no scholar could resolve the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the ברייתא was difficult for רבה בר ירמיה?

steps.title: First guess: why is שביעית more lenient than חול המועד?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests that the problem might be why removing worms and placing manure is allowed in שביעית but forbidden on מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the problem is מועד compared with שביעית: why is it allowed in שביעית and forbidden on מועד?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tests his first guess about the difficulty. The next step will knock it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows tending a tree's wound in שביעית but forbids it on מועד. That could look backwards, because שביעית is a whole year of agricultural restriction. רבינא raises this only to test it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This opens a suggestion that is often rejected.
חול המועד, the middle days of the festival.
The seventh year, when working the land is restricted.

phrases.english: If you say that the Festival compared to the Sabbatical Year
is difficult for him —
what is different about the Sabbatical Year that it is permitted,
and what is different about the Festival that it is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מוֹעֵד אַשְּׁבִיעִית קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first possible answer to the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difficulty might be the difference between שביעית and מועד.

steps.title: Rejected: חול המועד forbids even mere effort
steps.stepSummary: That cannot be the difficulty. שביעית forbids only real agricultural labor, while מועד forbids even ordinary effort.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? In שביעית the Torah forbade only labor, and effort is allowed. On מועד even effort is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows that the first guess is no real question, so it cannot be what bothered רבה בר ירמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two prohibitions work differently. שביעית bans only agricultural מלאכה, and tending a wound is just effort, so it is allowed. מועד bans even טירחא, so the ברייתא's ruling makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? This is a way of rejecting a comparison.
Effort or exertion that falls short of real labor.
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?!
The Sabbatical Year: the Merciful One forbade labor,
but exertion is permitted;
the Festival: even exertion is also forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty guessed in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the difficulty is שביעית compared with מועד.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two have different scopes: שביעית bans only labor, while מועד bans even effort.

steps.title: Second guess: why is manure allowed but pruning forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests that the problem might be why placing manure is permitted in שביעית while pruning is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps manuring compared with pruning is the difficulty: why is manuring allowed and pruning forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tries a second guess about the difficulty. The next step will reject this one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both actions involve treating a tree, yet the ברייתא treats them differently. רבינא tests whether this difference is what bothered רבה בר ירמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This introduces a new suggestion after the last one failed.
Placing manure on a tree's wound.

phrases.english: Rather, placing manure compared to pruning
is difficult for him:
what is different about placing manure that it is permitted,
and what is different about pruning that it is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא זִיהוּם אַגִּיזּוּם קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 rejected the first guess, this offers a second one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difficulty might be manuring compared with pruning.

steps.title: Rejected: manure saves the tree, pruning improves it
steps.stepSummary: That cannot be the difficulty either. Manuring keeps the tree alive, so it is allowed. Pruning makes the tree grow better, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? Manuring keeps the tree alive and is allowed. Pruning strengthens the tree and is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows that the second guess is also easy to answer, so it cannot be the real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step brings in a key principle for שביעית. Work that only keeps a tree from dying is permitted, while work that improves the tree is forbidden. This distinction becomes important in the following steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeping a tree alive or preserving it.

steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between preserving and improving is the tool רבינא uses in the following steps to answer the next contradictions.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?!
Placing manure is to preserve the tree, and it is permitted;
pruning is to strengthen the tree, and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty guessed in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the difficulty is manuring compared with pruning.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two have different purposes: one preserves the tree and the other improves it.

steps.title: Third guess: the משנה forbids manure during שביעית
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the difficulty is a contradiction. The ברייתא allows manuring in שביעית, but a משנה in שביעית allows manuring young trees only until ראש השנה of the seventh year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps the problem is manure compared with manure. The ברייתא teaches that one may remove worms and place manure in שביעית. But a משנה teaches that one may manure saplings, bind them, trim their tops, build shelters for them and water them until ראש השנה. Until ראש השנה, yes; during שביעית itself, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a third guess, and this time it is a real contradiction between two sources about placing manure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly permits זיהום during שביעית. The משנה says one may manure 'until ראש השנה', which implies that it is forbidden once the seventh year begins. These two sources seem to clash directly.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction against it from another source.
Until ראש השנה, meaning the start of the seventh year.

phrases.english: Rather, placing manure compared to placing manure
is difficult for him,
as it teaches: one may remove worms and place manure during the Sabbatical Year,
and they raised a contradiction: one may place manure on saplings,
and bind them, and trim their tops,
and make shelters for them,
and water them until Rosh HaShana —
until Rosh HaShana, yes,
during the Sabbatical Year, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, זִיהוּם אַזִּיהוּם קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 rejected the second guess, this offers a third, a real clash between sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's permission to place manure during שביעית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words 'until ראש השנה' imply that manuring is forbidden during the seventh year itself.

steps.title: Rejected: there are two kinds of manuring
steps.stepSummary: Even this can be answered. Just as רב עוקבא בר חמא said there are two kinds of hoeing, there may be two kinds of manuring: one that preserves the tree, which is allowed, and one that improves it, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is like רב עוקבא בר חמא, who said there are two kinds of hoeing. One strengthens the tree and is forbidden, and one closes cracks in the ground and is allowed. So too there are two kinds of manuring. One preserves the trees and is allowed, and one strengthens the trees and is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the contradiction, which shows that this third guess also cannot be the difficulty that 'no scholar could solve.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא speaks about manure that saves the tree, so it is allowed. The משנה speaks about manure that improves the tree, so it is forbidden. The rule from step 10 together with רב עוקבא בר חמא's model removes the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps. This introduces a possible answer that undoes a question.
Kinds of hoeing or loosening the soil.
To close up cracks in the ground.

steps.whatToRemember: The first three guesses all fail. The first two are no real question, and the third is answered with 'two kinds of manuring.' The key rule is that preserving a tree is allowed in שביעית while improving it is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: This step does not solve רבה בר ירמיה's puzzle. It only shows that this guess cannot be what bothered him, since it has an easy answer.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is like Rav Ukva bar Ḥama,
as Rav Ukva bar Ḥama said:
There are two kinds of hoeing,
one to strengthen the tree, and it is forbidden,
and one to close up cracks, and it is permitted.
So too, there are two kinds of placing manure,
one to preserve the trees, and it is permitted,
and one to strengthen the trees, and it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 11, which rules it out as the hidden difficulty.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the difficulty is the ברייתא's manuring compared with the משנה's manuring.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two sources may speak about different kinds of manuring, one that preserves and one that improves, just like the two kinds of hoeing.

steps.title: Maybe the problem is two rulings about smearing oil
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests that בר ירמיה was bothered by a contradiction. A ברייתא allows smearing oil on a pruned tree in שביעית. A משנה in שביעית allows smearing oil on unripe figs only until ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps the problem for him was one ruling about smearing against another ruling about smearing. The ברייתא teaches that one may smear oil on the pruned place of a tree both on חול המועד and in שביעית. But a משנה says that one may smear oil on unripe figs, pierce them, and fill them with oil until ראש השנה. That implies: until ראש השנה, yes, but in שביעית itself, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more guess about what bothered בר ירמיה. It points to a contradiction between two sources about smearing oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows smearing oil in שביעית. The משנה in שביעית limits smearing oil to before ראש השנה, which suggests it is forbidden in שביעית itself. If both talk about the same kind of smearing, they seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: They fatten or fill (the fruit) with oil
And they raised a contradiction: introduces a source that seems to clash

phrases.english: Rather, smearing against smearing
was difficult for him
As it teaches: one may smear oil on the pruned place
both on חול המועד and in שביעית
And they contrasted it with: one may smear the unripe figs
and pierce them and fill them with oil
until ראש השנה
phrases.notes: This is the ראש השנה that starts the seventh year.

phrases.aramaic: עַד רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אִין, בִּשְׁבִיעִית לָא!
phrases.english: Until ראש השנה, yes; in שביעית, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, סִיכָה אַסִּיכָה קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the manuring contradiction was answered in step 12, the גמרא tries another contradiction, this time about smearing oil.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא permitting smearing oil in שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in שביעית implies that smearing oil is forbidden once the seventh year begins, which seems to contradict the ברייתא.

steps.title: Oil on a tree differs from oil on fruit
steps.stepSummary: The two cases are not alike. Oil on a pruned tree keeps the tree alive, so it is allowed. Oil on figs fattens the fruit, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable?! Here, the oil keeps the tree alive, so it is permitted. There, it fattens the fruit, so it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the smearing contradiction. The two cases serve different purposes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same idea as before: keeping a tree alive is allowed in שביעית, but improving it is forbidden. Smearing the cut spot only preserves the tree. Smearing figs makes the fruit bigger, which is real improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? (the cases are different)

phrases.english: Are they comparable?!
Here it keeps the tree alive, so it is permitted
There it fattens the fruit, so it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the smearing-against-smearing contradiction as the source of בר ירמיה's puzzlement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction ignores that one smearing preserves the tree while the other improves the fruit.

steps.title: The real puzzle: smearing allowed but manuring forbidden on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא בריה דרב אשי explains what truly bothered בר ירמיה. On חול המועד, smearing oil is allowed and manuring is forbidden, even though both only keep the tree alive. That is why he said no carpenter could solve it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סמא, son of רב אשי, said to רבינא: What bothered בר ירמיה was smearing on חול המועד against manuring on חול המועד. After all, this keeps the tree alive and that keeps the tree alive. So why is this one permitted and that one forbidden? That is why he said: there is no carpenter or son of a carpenter who can take this apart.
steps.whatsHappening: After several guesses were rejected, רב סמא gives the final answer. He explains what puzzled בר ירמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers used the difference between keeping a tree alive and improving it. On חול המועד, both smearing oil and manuring only keep the tree alive, so that difference does not help here. Since no reason can be found for treating them differently, בר ירמיה said that no expert could solve it.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, since (introduces an obvious premise)
Can take it apart, meaning solve it

steps.whatToRemember: The search ends here. On חול המועד, smearing oil is permitted and manuring is forbidden, even though both only preserve the tree. בר ירמיה found this unsolvable.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא
phrases.english: רב סמא, son of רב אשי, said to רבינא

phrases.aramaic: בַּר יִרְמְיָה סִיכָה דְּמוֹעֵד אַזִּיהוּם דְּמוֹעֵד
phrases.english: For בר ירמיה, smearing on חול המועד against manuring on חול המועד
was what was difficult for him
After all, this keeps it alive and that keeps it alive
what is different about this one, that it is permitted
and what is different about that one, that it is forbidden?
That is why he said to him

phrases.aramaic: לֵית נַגָּר וְלָא בַּר נַגָּר דְּיִפְרְקִינַּהּ
phrases.english: There is no carpenter nor son of a carpenter who can take it apart
phrases.notes: A saying that means no expert, and no student of an expert, can solve it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all the earlier guesses were rejected, this gives the accepted explanation of בר ירמיה's puzzle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly did בר ירמיה find unsolvable?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On חול המועד, smearing oil is permitted and manuring is forbidden, though both only preserve the tree, and no reason for the difference is apparent.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The difference between smearing and manuring on חול המועד remains without an explanation.

steps.title: Breaking or throwing a stick before an idol
steps.stepSummary: רב rules about an idol that is worshipped with a stick. Someone who breaks a stick before it is liable. Someone who throws a stick before it is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If an idol is worshipped with a stick, and someone broke a stick before it, he is liable. If he threw a stick before it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a ruling about an idol whose normal worship uses a stick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking and throwing are not the usual way this idol is worshipped. Even so, רב says breaking makes a person liable and throwing does not. The next steps explain why.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב said
An idol that is worshipped with a stick
if he broke a stick before it, he is liable
if he threw a stick before it, he is exempt

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion about trees ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking a stick before a stick-worshipped idol makes one liable; throwing a stick before it does not.

steps.title: Why isn't throwing like sprinkling blood?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא: if breaking counts because it resembles שחיטה, throwing should count because it resembles זריקה of the blood on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: What is different about breaking? It counts because it is like slaughtering. Throwing is also like sprinkling blood!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב's ruling. He says throwing should make a person liable just like breaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumes breaking makes a person liable because it looks like שחיטה, one of the Temple services. Throwing also looks like a Temple service, the זריקה of the blood. So he asks why throwing should be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling or throwing the blood of an offering on the מזבח

phrases.english: אביי said to רבא
What is different about breaking
that it is like slaughtering?

phrases.aramaic: זָרַק נָמֵי הֲוָה לֵיהּ כְּעֵין זְרִיקָה!
phrases.english: Throwing is also like sprinkling!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא: מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction רב made in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's exemption for throwing a stick
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If resemblance to שחיטה makes breaking punishable, resemblance to זריקה should make throwing punishable too.

steps.title: Real זריקה must scatter
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that זריקה of blood spreads out and scatters. A stick that is thrown stays whole, so it does not resemble זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I need a throwing that splits apart, and that is not present here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's challenge. Throwing a stick is not truly like the Temple זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When blood is thrown on the מזבח, it splashes and spreads. A thrown stick stays in one piece, so it lacks the feature that makes זריקה what it is. Breaking does look like שחיטה, so רב's distinction stands.
steps.whatToRemember: An act counts as resembling a Temple service only if it shares that service's key feature. Breaking resembles שחיטה. Throwing a whole stick does not resemble זריקה, because זריקה scatters.

phrases.english: He said to him
I need a throwing that breaks apart, and that is not here
phrases.notes: Blood thrown on the מזבח splashes and spreads, but a thrown stick lands in one piece.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the essential feature of the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any throwing resembles זריקה of blood, so throwing a stick should make a person liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: זריקה requires something that scatters. A whole stick does not scatter, so throwing it is exempt.

steps.title: אביי quotes a ברייתא about excrement and urine
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a challenge to רבא by quoting a ברייתא about someone who feeds an idol excrement or pours a chamber pot of urine before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: One who fed it excrement, or who poured a chamber pot of urine before it as a libation...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to challenge רבא's answer by quoting a ברייתא. This line only sets up the cases; the ברייתא's ruling and the point of the challenge come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a thrown stick is not like זריקה because it stays whole and does not scatter. אביי now brings cases that look nothing like the real service in the בית המקדש: feeding excrement and pouring urine. He is getting ready to use the ruling on these cases to test רבא's way of comparing acts to the service of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Poured as a libation, like pouring wine on the מזבח

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי challenging רבא's answer from the last step.

phrases.english: One who fed it excrement,
or who poured as a libation before it
a chamber pot of urine —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge, based on a ברייתא, against רבא's answer in Step 18 that a thrown stick is not like זריקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that throwing a stick is exempt because it does not resemble the scattering זריקה of blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא lists acts that are not like the service of the בית המקדש. Its ruling, given in the next part of the text, will be used to test רבא's method of comparing acts to the service of the מזבח.
